title: State Machine Leak on Network Disconnect
damaged_code:
```rust
// Custom network state:
int rtrg_status; // If connection fails, status is left in CLOSING forever
```
pattern: Handcrafting low-level network state transitions without binding resource deallocation to connection teardown events.
why_bad: If a client disconnects abruptly, the internal state machine remains in an intermediate state, keeping allocated memory, ports, or handles open indefinitely, leading to resource exhaustion.
detection: State variables mutated in network callback paths without a corresponding cleanup callback on socket drop.
counterexample: Standard futures-based or event-driven frameworks where dropping the connection wrapper automatically drops and cancels the inner state.
fix: Associate the lifecycle of the state machine directly with the lifetime of the underlying network connection using RAII, ensuring state teardown occurs when the socket drops.
